items.text: This makes the filament an excellent choice for applications requiring effective current conduction.
The filament is based on a durable ASA polymer enriched with carbon nanotubes (CNT), which provide very low surface resistivity – around 40 Ω.
Matte finish to reduce visible layers
Closed chamber recommended for larger prints
Higher temperatures improve the dispersion of carbon nanotubes withinthe model’s structure, resulting in lower volume resistivity.

For the user, this means that printingcomponentsrequiring maximum conductivity is best achieved at higher extrusion temperatures (up to 290°C), provided that the printer's hardware supports such settings.

items.text: Good resistance: water, aqueous salt solutions, detergent solutions, dilute acids and alkalis (overview table, column SAN, ABS, MABS, ASA)
items.note: Key: + resistant over a period of months to years; 0 limited resistance (some swelling, solvation or environmental stress cracking possible); - not resistant (severe swelling, decomposition, solvation or environmental stress cracking). Where the 20 °C and 50 °C ratings differ, the verdict here is limited and both ratings are given. Column read: Luran S (ASA). BASF was the producer at publication (2002); the resins are now INEOS Styrolution.
